# DaisySP provenance

Upstream: https://github.com/electro-smith/DaisySP commit `2c72eaf9eac5fc0dca1919d65d606da907832618`. `Source/Control/adsr.{h,cpp}` and `Source/Synthesis/oscillator.{h,cpp}` are the upstream MIT-licensed modules; `LICENSE` retains upstream's complete notices. The `Utility/dsp.h` in this directory is a minimal compatibility subset, because upstream's utility header includes C++ standard library features unavailable in the Circle configuration.

Local changes: oscillator state initialization sets the polyBLEP integrator history to zero; an enum cast avoids a compiler warning. In ADSR, `log(1/e)` is replaced with its mathematical value `-1.0f` because the freestanding C library does not define `M_E`. `src/daisy_synth.h` composes the imported modules into a two-oscillator monophonic voice. `src/polyblep_saw.h` is an earlier, separately adapted excerpt of the upstream oscillator. No Raspberry Pi or MK3 hardware performance measurements have been performed.

For the groovebox insert hot path, `Svf::ProcessMode` performs the same two filter passes while computing only the selected output; `Overdrive::ProcessInline` is an inline equivalent of the original `Process`. The original methods remain available. `Svf::CopyCoefficientsFrom` shares calculated coefficients across stereo channels without copying filter history.

The first future-feature wave enables `Source/Filters/ladder.{h,cpp}` from the **same pinned commit** above, already present in the local DaisySP source cache. No new library or upstream revision is introduced. These files retain Richard van Hoesel / Infrasonic Audio's MIT notices; this is `LadderFilter`, not the LGPL MoogLadder module. For the freestanding target, `std::array<float,5>` is replaced by a local C array and const pointer, and utility max/min calls use `fmaxf`/`fminf`. Init initializes drive before gain setup and clears filter history so reusing a voice is deterministic. Oversampling and filter equations are unchanged.

Wave 3 enables `Source/Synthesis/harmonic_osc.h` from the same pinned local source cache, byte-for-byte unchanged (MIT, Electrosmith / Emilie Gillet). No new upstream/library is introduced. The voice adapter explicitly clears the numeric-only object representation before Init, which reads existing fields while assigning frequency/index; the upstream empty user constructor does not guarantee zero initialization. Spectrum macros, ADSR and the phase-distortion voice live outside the vendor file.

Synth extensions E3 enables Source/Synthesis/formantosc.{h,cpp} and vosim.{h,cpp} byte-for-byte from the same pinned 2c72eaf cache. Each retains the Electrosmith / Emilie Gillet MIT notice. Initialization of numeric state is in the adapter, not a vendor patch. File SHA256 is recorded in docs/validation/synth-extensions/e3-vendor.json.

Synth extensions E6 enables Effects/pitchshifter.h, Utility/delayline.h and Control/phasor.{h,cpp} unmodified from the same MIT pinned cache. SHA256: docs/validation/synth-extensions/e6-vendor.json. The adapter zeros numeric vendor state before Init, fixes delay length to 2048 and Fun to zero, and masks stale history for 2048 samples plus a 256-sample fade. Vendor myrand remains single audio-owner state. No new LGPL modules.
